name: Thorns and spines
log: A spine finds your hand. The cut is small, rude, and exactly where you will use it.
journal: Thorns, cactus spines, and torn aluminum all open the skin. They are not dramatic. They are how an infection starts if you are careless in the wash.

name: Snakebite
log: A buzz, then a punch in the calf. The snake is already gone. The bite stays.
journal: Snakes own the shade under rock, especially morning and dusk. A bite is a slow emergency. Treat it with a kit or lose the next day to the venom's clock.

name: Scorpion sting
log: You move a stone and the stone disagrees. The sting is a hot nail in the wrist.
journal: Scorpions shelter in shoes, sleeves, and under rocks, especially at night. A sting ruins sleep and steals hours. Shake out cloth. A fire at camp keeps most of them off you.

name: Sunburn
log: The sun finds the back of your neck and writes on it. You will feel this tomorrow.
journal: Open travel in the hot hours burns skin fast. Sunburn shortens the next day and makes heat worse. Shade, a shelter, and a creosote poultice are the answers. Heroics are not.

name: A bad step
log: A stone rolls under your boot. You go down hard.
journal: Loose stone cuts and sprains. The ridge charges the highest toll. Go up with water, daylight that is not noon, and enough health to pay for a mistake.
